decision.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
decision.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground separately, including substantial foreground structures. Chalk contours, broken or layered strokes, and rubbed shading may qualify; simplified forms and smooth sky passages are allowed. For broad rubbed passages, look for boundaries, layering or pigment variation that constructs the depicted terrain, vegetation, structures or ground planes, rather than relying solely on source-derived tonal fields. Reduced photographic detail, diagonal streaking, grain or smearing alone does not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas remain photographic modeling softened by blur or texture, even when nearby vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Do not require every area to contain discrete strokes or regard retained composition as evidence of failure. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
